summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted due to worsening epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the left flank, shortly after a prior discharge for similar symptoms. With a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube placement following a previous anastomotic ulcer, she was managed conservatively. A CT scan showed no intra-abdominal infection or fluid collection, with stable post-surgical changes. She remained on tube feeds using Vivonex, which was well tolerated, and received IV morphine for pain, later transitioned to oral Dilaudid and Tylenol. After a Fleet’s enema relieved constipation and bloating, her pain improved significantly. She was discharged home in stable condition, tolerating feeds, ambulating independently, and with clear mental status. Discharge instructions included continuing sucralfate, PPI, rifaximin, and G-tube site care, with follow-up planned.
